_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Austria covering Celtic/Roman Noricum, Carolingian Ostmark (Eastern March), Babenberg dynasty, Habsburg dynasty (1282-1918, 640 years, Europe's greatest dynasty), Holy Roman Empire centre, Reformation/Counter-Reformation, Ottoman sieges of Vienna (1529, 1683), Maria Theresa reforms, Napoleonic Wars, Congress of Vienna 1815 (Metternich), Austrian Empire, Austro-Hungarian Compromise 1867 (Dual Monarchy), WWI assassination of Franz Ferdinand (Sarajevo 1914), Republic 1918, Anschluss 1938 (Nazi annexation), WWII, Allied occupation 1945-55, neutrality (1955 State Treaty), EU accession 1995, and cultural legacy (Mozart, Beethoven, Freud, Habsburg Empire).

religion.note: Catholic historically dominant (Counter-Reformation victory); declining rapidly; Muslim community (Turkish/Bosnian immigration); Orthodox (Serbian/Romanian); Protestant (Augsburg Confession, Burgenland); no religion growing fast; religion still culturally embedded (Christmas markets, church tax)

ethnic_groups.name: Austrian/German-speaking
ethnic_groups.notes: German-speaking; distinct national identity (not German, despite shared language); Austrian German dialect; Habsburg multicultural heritage; 'first victim' myth (post-WWII, debated)

ethnic_groups.name: Croatian (Burgenland)

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Hungarian (Burgenland), Slovene (Carinthia), Polish, Czech (Habsburg legacy); Roma/Sinti

independence.from: Allied occupation (State Treaty); republic since 1918 (Habsburg dissolution)

country_profile.notes_unique: Habsburg dynasty (1282-1918, 640 years, Holy Roman Emperors, ruled half of Europe, 'Austria est imperare orbi universo'); Vienna (imperial capital, cultural zenith, Ringstraße, coffeehouses); Congress of Vienna 1815 (Metternich, reshaped Europe post-Napoleon); Austro-Hungarian Empire (1867-1918, Dual Monarchy, 52M subjects); WWI trigger (assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, June 28, 1914, Sarajevo); Anschluss 1938 (Nazi annexation, Hitler Austrian-born from Braunau am Inn); Holocaust complicity ('first victim' myth debated); neutrality since 1955 (not NATO, Vienna = UN/OSCE/OPEC headquarters); musical capital of world (Mozart, Haydn, Schubert, Strauss, Mahler, Bruckner; Vienna Philharmonic, State Opera); Freud (psychoanalysis, Vienna); Klimt/Schiele (art); Alpine skiing nation; Sound of Music; 12 UNESCO World Heritage Sites

910.name: Hallstatt Celtic Culture & Roman Noricum
910.description: The Hallstatt culture represents one of Europe's earliest identifiable Celtic civilisations, centred in the salt-mining region of upper Austria. The subsequent Roman province of Noricum became a vital frontier territory supplying iron and gold to the empire.
